Blench, Roger M. 2021. The phonology, noun-classes and pronominal system of the Idũ (Dũya) language of Central Nigeria, including a re-analysis of the tonal system. Draft circulated for comment ('This version: Jos, September 16, 2021'). Cambridge: Kay Williamson Educational Foundation. ii+15 pp. Posted on Academia.edu, item 52552119 (uploaded 2021-09-16).
sources.note: Sec. 3.3 Tones (pp.10-11) quotes Marggrander (2019: 33 ff.) - 'two distinctive tone levels' H and L with 'non-phonemic mid tones.. analyzed as downstepped high tones' - calls this surprising since most neighbouring languages have three level tones, and argues that Idũ has THREE level tones (High marked acute, Mid unmarked, Low grave) plus glide tones (rising Low-High, falling High-Low, falling Mid-Low) that 'presumably arise from sequences of level tones'. sources.note: A German-language comparative study of Plateau languages (noun-class systems, sound correspondences, wordlists) in which Lungu (= Idũ) is one of the sampled varieties with 'minimal' coverage per Glottolog's description type; Gerhardt transcribes tone in his Plateau data, so tone-marked Lungu forms and possibly a short note on its tone levels are likely, but no dedicated Lungu tone analysis is expected; pages for Lungu not located.
